Title: Instance econ probe — uniform sampling audit
Context: This is a working audit of per-token economics and perf/W observations for a 7B family-like generation workload (baseline: redwood-7b-sim). Purpose: quick heuristics we can drop into Optimize and hand to infra/product for recommendations. Not a final benchmark; sampling-based (uniform over common seq lengths) and contains measurement notes, quick calculations, and follow-ups.
Assumptions & test bed:
- Model: redwood-7b-sim (FP16/qt8 where noted)
- Runtime: internal inference runtime v1.9 (CUDA 12.2, cuBLAS/cublasLt kernels, Triton-like batching)
- Warmup: 120s steady-state, then 3x 60s measurement windows
- Measurement: nvidia-smi power sampling + runtime counters, p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec measured at generator-level
- Pricing: assumed hourly GPU rates (on-reserve equivalent) used for comparative math only: A10 $0.50/hr, L4 $1.20/hr, A100 $3.60/hr, H100 $5.40/hr
- Power draw (measured under test workload): A10 150W, L4 120W, A100 400W, H100 500W
- Batch config: generation batch=4 for seq512, batch=2 for seq2048 (memory-limited)
- Sampling: uniform across sequence lengths [64, 256, 512, 1024, 2048] but table below summarizes 512 and 2048 as representative
Interpretation / immediate takeaways:
- H100 shows lowest $/token in these sample windows despite the highest hourly cost; its throughput advantage dominates for steady high-concurrency generation.
- L4/A100 tradeoffs: L4 can be more cost-effective at smaller loads or when batch consolidation is good (higher perf/W), but in our samples A100 beats L4 on $/token at seq512 and ties at longer seq once batching improves.
- A10 remains attractive for very low-scale workloads or where absolute throughput isn't required; its perf/W is low but nominal $/token can be similar for short sequences.
Caveats & measurement notes:
- These are single-GPU numbers for a single model; multi-GPU scaling and multi-tenant scheduling will change economics.
- Pricing used is illustrative; market/commitment pricing and burst vs reserved capacity will shift cost curves.
- We did not measure RPC/host CPU overhead for tiny-batch RPC-heavy workloads which penalize small GPUs.
- We did limited experiments with int8/q8 kernels: quantization reduced per-token runtime by ~10–20% on A10/L4 but required slightly larger batch sizes to be stable.
Recommendations / action items:
- Short-term (product): Default Optimize recommendation: "H100 for sustained high-throughput gen; L4 reserved for mid-tier latency-sensitive thin-tail workloads; A10 for dev/smaller dev/test clusters" — include confidence bands and cost sensitivity toggles.
- Mid-term (engineering): Run a full factorial benchmark across batch sizes [1,2,4,8] × seq_length [64,256,512,1024,2048] × quant modes [fp16,qt8] and produce a lookup table for routing logic.
- Instrumentation: Add tokens/sec/K/Vcache hit tags to telemetry to attribute token costs by route.
Open questions / follow-ups:
- Run same sweep on redwood-13b-sim and on streaming workloads (where latency matters more than throughput).
- Measure tail-latency when consolidating many small requests; small-instance math may break if RPC dominates.
- Validate with real pricing (cloud spot and reserved) and with Dedicated unit economics (fixed monthly amortized infra cost).
